chunks: And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Al-ʿĪṣ ibn Al-Qāsim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who advanced dirhams to another man for wheat, then when the term became due, he did not have food, but he found that he had animals, slaves, and goods. Is it halal (permissible) for him to take those items from his property in exchange for his food?
He said: Yes, he may specify such-and-such for such-and-such sāʿs.

key_terms.أَسْلَفَ: advanced payment in a salam transaction
key_terms.الْأَجَلُ: the fixed due term of the contract
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: silver coin currency used as payment
key_terms.صَاعًا: a measured unit of volume for commodities
key_terms.طَعَامٌ: food commodity owed in the transaction

ai.seo_question: Is it halal (permissible) to take goods, animals, or slaves instead of food owed in an advance-payment contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding an advance-payment sale involving wheat when the seller cannot deliver the food at the due date. It permits taking other goods in exchange, provided the substitute items and their corresponding measure are clearly specified.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3939 - Safwan bin Yahya narrated from Al-Ays bin Al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who had advanced dirhams to another man for wheat. When the due date arrived, the debtor did not have any food but had animals, slaves, and goods.
I asked: "Is it permissible for him to take these items in place of the wheat owed to him?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes, he may specify such and such items for such and such a measure."
